notes.title: Early Access Release September 16
notes.content:
[h2]Pompeii: The Legacy – Coming to Early Access on September 16![/h2][p]Hey everyone![/p][p]I’m incredibly excited to finally share the news — [b]Pompeii: The Legacy[/b] will launch into [b]Early Access on Steam on September 16, 2025[/b]!
As a solo developer, this moment means the world to me. Thank you all for following the journey so far, whether you played the demo, shared your feedback, or just wishlisted the game; every bit of support matters.[/p][previewyoutube="RQqLH4p9Pqk;full"][/previewyoutube][hr][/hr][h2]Your Legacy, Forged in the Shadow of Vesuvius[/h2][p]In [i]Pompeii: The Legacy[/i], you're not just building a city, you’re shaping the story of a Roman family across generations. Your decisions in politics, religion, trade, military affairs, and aesthetics shape not only the lives of your citizens, but the very fabric of Pompeii itself.
The game draws from real historical events, but leaves plenty of room for you to rewrite history in your own way.[/p][carousel][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45181346/9f76a33189af9f7735a3ff07759ce5765b5233fb.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45181346/8a0de6b80c2f2ffc4c1f69a034932e1cbeb610e7.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45181346/15f5537cbd2b188c519cb73a96e7618db840fa0f.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45181346/bd0b6f5c9ac8a6c6abcd7638f28f6d4b5af9cc80.jpg"][/img][/carousel][hr][/hr][h2]What to Expect in Early Access[/h2][p]The Early Access version will include [b]three game modes[/b]:[/p][list][*][p]A fully playable [b]campaign[/b] with narrative quests and progression[/p][/*][*][p]A [b]sandbox mode[/b] for open-ended city building with challenges[/p][/*][*][p]A [b]creative mode[/b] for relaxed, penalty-free construction[/p][/*][/list][p]Throughout Early Access, I’ll be continuing development on new features, improving balance and visuals, and integrating your feedback into the game’s evolution.

While the core systems will be fully functional at launch, [b]the military gameplay will initially be limited to its basic form[/b]. More advanced combat mechanics, including battles will be introduced gradually throughout Early Access.[/p][p]A detailed [b]roadmap[/b] outlining planned updates and timelines will be published shortly before the EA release, so you'll have a clear view of what’s coming next.[/p][hr][/hr][h2]And That’s Just the Beginning[/h2][p]Over the coming weeks, I’ll be sharing several [b]developer blogs[/b] right here on Steam covering key areas of the game:[/p][list][*][p]The [b]production system[/b] and resource chains[/p][/*][*][p]How [b]trade[/b] works, both land and sea[/p][/*][*][p]The [b]military system[/b] (and how you can also pursue a peaceful route)[/p][/*][*][p]UI and UX changes based on feedback[/p][/*][*][p]And later on, support for [b]modding[/b], giving even more creative freedom to the community[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][p]Once again, thank you for being here and helping bring Pompeii to life.
I truly hope you’ll enjoy what’s coming, and I can’t wait to hear your thoughts when the Early Access version goes live!
[/p][p]See you soon in Pompeii!
[/p][p]Zeljko
Solo dev @ Siscia Games

[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2632240/Pompeii_The_Legacy/"][/dynamiclink][/p]

notes.title: Steam Next Fest Demo Now Live
notes.content:
[h2]Pompeii: The Legacy – Final Next Fest Demo Is Now Live!
[/h2][p]The time has come – the [b]Next Fest demo[/b] for [b][i]Pompeii: The Legacy[/i][/b] is now live![/p][p]Whether you played the earlier playtest or you’re just now discovering the game, this [b]final version of the demo[/b] gives you a much deeper look into what I’ve been working on over the past months.
[/p][h3]What’s New Since the Playtest?[/h3][p]I’ve added and improved a lot since the early version. Here's what's new:[/p][p]	🔹 [b]Fully Playable Sandbox Mode[/b]
		You can now build without restrictions, shaping your city however you want.[/p][p]	🔹 [b]Trade System Enabled[/b]
		Set up trade routes, manage your ships, and exchange resources with other Roman cities.[/p][p]	🔹 [b]Expanded Research Tree[/b]
		A significantly larger tech tree is now available, allowing for deeper development paths.[/p][p]	🔹 [b]New Social Research Branch[/b]
		Unlock privileges and societal upgrades that affect your citizens and city's direction.[/p][p]	🔹 [b]New Buildings & Decorations[/b]
		A range of new production buildings and visual decorations have been added.[/p][p]	🔹 [b]Improved Hand-Painted Map[/b]
		The world map now features updated visuals and better detail.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p]During the course of [b]Next Fest[/b], I’ll be releasing [b]at least two major updates[/b] for the demo, each introducing new features, improvements, and content. I’ll also be paying close attention to your feedback, suggestions, and critiques, because they truly help shape [b][i]Pompeii: The Legacy[/i][/b] into something better with every step. Your voice matters, and I want this game to grow into something we’ll all be proud of.[/p][hr][/hr][p]Thank you so much for the support. If you enjoy the demo, [b]please consider wishlisting the game[/b], it really helps me as a solo developer.[/p][p][/p][p][b][i]Pompeii: The Legacy[/i][/b] is just getting started. I hope you enjoy what’s here, and what’s coming next![/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2632240/Pompeii_The_Legacy/"][/dynamiclink][/p]

notes.title: The Final Playtest Before Steam Next Fest
notes.content:
[h2]The Final Playtest Before Next Fest[/h2]

The new [b]Pompeii: The Legacy[/b] playtest is live, and it marks the last public test before the upcoming press demo version launching on [b]May 29th[/b].

This version includes numerous improvements based on feedback from the first playtest:
[list]
[*] A completely overhauled Menu UI with visual polish and easier navigation
[*] Brand new family & symbol customization for your citizens
[*] Enhanced visuals and refined gameplay balance
[*] A reworked system for handling grain fields, with vineyards and olive groves coming in the demo
[*] A shorter campaign slice, missing a few late quests that will appear in the demo
[*] Sandbox mode and trade system are currently locked, but both will be fully available in the demo
[*] A new, more intuitive tutorial with UI highlights will also be included in the demo version
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45181346/f55d76f6baa22790e18c75674400504264d2780f.jpg[/img]

I also hope players will enjoy some of the new buildings already added, and those coming in the demo. From the warmth of the Bakery, to the practical calm of the Herbalist Garden, the textile bustle of the Clothing Factory, and the iconic relaxation of the Bathhouse, these additions aim to bring more life and depth to your Pompeii. They're not just functional, they carry personality, and I can't wait to see how you'll build with them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45181346/807538d352cf204fbac2238f79ecd535620b44da.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45181346/b768efbade8a427bf55e403df8b79346a25987a1.jpg[/img]

[h2]Coming Soon: Steam Next Fest[/h2]

[b]Pompeii: The Legacy[/b] will officially take part in [b]Steam Next Fest[/b], starting [b]June 9[/b]. The upcoming Next Fest demo will offer even more content, features, and polish, and will be available to both players and press. Be sure to wishlist the game and stay tuned as I prepare to showcase a deeper look into ancient city-building, survival, and legacy.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2632240/Pompeii_The_Legacy/

notes.title: Pre-Alpha Footage & Steam Playtest
notes.content:
[h3]Pure Gameplay[/h3]

For a while now, many of you have been asking to see more of [b]Pompeii: The Legacy[/b] in action. Instead of a cinematic trailer, I’ve decided to do something different—give you [b]30 minutes of pure, unfiltered gameplay footage[/b] from the current pre-alpha version. No scripted sequences, no heavy editing—just the game as it is right now.

Reaching this stage is a huge milestone for me as a solo developer, especially while working on my own game engine. Balancing both development and marketing has been a demanding journey, but seeing [b]Pompeii: The Legacy[/b] take shape makes it all worthwhile. With this gameplay footage, I feel like I’ve hit the first truly major goal—being able to show the game in action and let you experience what I’ve been building.

[previewyoutube=9wZy4xUosFY;full][/previewyoutube]

This footage showcases the core city-building mechanics, visuals, and atmosphere of [b]Pompeii: The Legacy[/b] in its current state. However, it's important to note that this is [b]not the final version[/b]—things are still evolving!

[h3]Looking Ahead: Steam Playtest Improvements[/h3]

The [b]Steam Playtest launches in mid-March[/b], and your feedback from this pre-alpha gameplay footage will be invaluable in shaping the final experience. If you haven't already, [b]sign up on Steam[/b] to be among the first to try it!

[b]Here’s what’s set to improve before the Playtest:[/b]

[list]
[*] [b]Enhanced Visuals[/b] – Expect more polished textures, refined lighting, and added environmental details to bring the city to life.
[*] [b]Gameplay Refinements[/b] – The game’s pacing will be adjusted, with faster construction times and a greater emphasis on bonuses & upgrades.
[*] [b]More Buildings[/b] – The Playtest will feature additional structures, including mines and metal processing buildings, expanding the depth of production chains.
[*] E[b]xpanded Citizen Needs[/b] – Hygiene will play a more significant role, introducing new buildings like barber shops and public latrines to maintain health and morale.
[*] [b]Trade System[/b] – Missing from the current footage, but fully implemented for the Playtest, allowing for economic strategy and trade between cities.
[*] [b]Military & City Defense[/b] – While not yet in-game, walls, soldiers, and combat mechanics are planned for post-Playtest development, adding another strategic layer to Pompeii’s survival.
[/list]

[h3]Thank You for Your Support![/h3]

A huge thanks to everyone following the journey of [b]Pompeii: The Legacy[/b]! Your enthusiasm and feedback mean the world, and I’m excited to share even more with you in the coming weeks. If you haven’t already, be sure to wishlist the game on Steam—it helps tremendously and ensures you won’t miss any future updates!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2632240/Pompeii_The_Legacy/

notes.title: Dev Blog 3: WhaleX Engine
notes.content:
[h2]Welcome to the Third Dev Blog![/h2]

[h3]Developing Pompeii: The Legacy in the WhaleX Engine[/h3]

In today's game development world, it's not common to see a developer creating their own game engine, especially with so many commercial engines readily available. However, [b]WhaleX Engine[/b] has been a passion project of mine for quite some time, designed to fit my specific needs as a solo developer. Built on [b]DirectX 11[/b] technology, [b]WhaleX Engine[/b] allows me to have full control over the development process of my upcoming city-building game, [b]Pompeii: The Legacy[/b].

In the following sections, I will explain several key features that are crucial to the development of the game. But first, I would like to list some of the notable features my engine possesses:

[list]
[*] Terrain size is 4 square kilometers (about 1.54 square miles)
[*] Up to 12 different materials on the terrain
[*] 6 materials support terrain displacement, with 3 of them providing detailed textures like small stones
[*] Sea and rivers are animated with Gerstner wave systems
[*] An optimized foliage system for adding grass, leaves, and small plants
[*] A weather system that enhances the atmosphere with rain, storms, and volcanic ash
[/list]

[h3]Terrain[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45181346/2377f6242c3d9f28ae5b4d7a9014c2ce71288ab1.jpg[/img]

One of the engine’s key strengths is its optimization for games with a top-down view, like city builders. I’ve developed several custom tools for terrain editing, texture painting, shoreline creation, and more. Currently, the engine supports up to 12 different textures for terrain, three of which allow displacement mapping. An additional three textures can have both displacement and detail mapping, allowing for small elements like pebbles to be painted onto the landscape, creating more intricate ground detail.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45181346/000a5035eab0b2231367ef0dc6e9706805af024e.jpg[/img]

The above image demonstrates how the detailed texture system adds small stones to the terrain. Along with this, [b]WhaleX Engine[/b] features an optimized system for adding grass and foliage without causing performance issues. The engine's editor allows for quick placement of larger plants like shrubs, trees, and environmental details such as fallen logs, mushrooms, and even Mediterranean plants like cacti and yucca.


[h3]Splines and regions[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45181346/fb60f3ed27aa2f0b5ddfab21bfa87bad71ac23a6.jpg[/img]

Another powerful feature of [b]WhaleX Engine[/b] is the ability to add various splines and definition regions, essential for designing interactive areas within the game world. These regions dictate where animals roam, where fish swim, and where players can mine resources. Additionally, the engine handles complex elements like water pumps for aqueducts and fertile zones for agriculture, offering a highly customizable game world.


[h3]Water system[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45181346/afcc9623c0be4bb41c203faeeac97700ad7b11fb.jpg[/img]

The next big feature in [b]WhaleX Engine[/b] is its water system. I’ve built an advanced system that simulates the dynamics of seas and rivers within the game. At its core is a Gerstner wave system, which realistically governs the ocean’s surface. The engine allows for the tweaking of various parameters: amplitude, frequency of waves, and color of rivers, shallow, and deep waters. You can also test how the sea behaves under different weather conditions, such as when rain hits the ocean’s surface.


[h3]Weather manipulation[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45181346/eddc025d217ca2d76f2a9baf7958068b5ba2d780.jpg[/img]

In [b]Pompeii: The Legacy[/b], players will experience a dynamic weather system that enhances immersion and gameplay challenges. Beyond sunny skies, the game features cloudy conditions, rainstorms, and even full-blown thunderstorms. The weather system also plays a critical role in volcanic activities, with ash filling the air during eruptions, small stones falling from the sky, and, in extreme cases, larger rocks descending as part of the catastrophic events. These atmospheric elements not only impact the visual ambiance but also bring new gameplay layers as players must adapt to the changing environment.


This level of flexibility within [b]WhaleX Engine[/b] allows me to create a game environment that feels authentic and immersive, pushing the boundaries of what's possible in a city-building game like [b]Pompeii: The Legacy[/b]. As development continues, I’m excited to keep refining these systems and expand the possibilities even further.

Stay tuned for more updates as I continue to push the limits of what [b]WhaleX Engine[/b] can do!
